## Analysis

**Data overview:** The training set (300 samples, targets 177–1900 MPa) covers many steel families. The pool of 34 candidates all belong to a carbon/chromium-steel family (Cr=13, C≈0.2, Ni/Mn/Si/Cu/Ti in narrow ranges), with variations mainly over Heat treatment step 2 (tempering) temperature and Aging treatment parameters.

**Model choice:** I compared RF, Extra Trees, Gradient/Histogram Boosting, kNN, and Ridge with 10-fold CV — Gradient Boosting was clearly best (R²≈0.78, MAE≈78 MPa, vs kNN R²≈0.59). On a held-out subset of pool-like family rows, Gradient Boosting also ranked best (Spearman=0.70).

**Key physical insight:** Within the candidate family, the dominant driver is Heat treatment step-2 (tempering) temperature — Spearman = −0.977 within the family subset: lower tempering temperature keeps yield strength much higher. Composition-wise, candidates with more Si/Mn/Ti/Cu (e.g., c006-type) rank above the leaner (Ni=0, Si=0.4) compositions. Aging-treatment candidates (temp > 0) generally scored lower.

**Final ensemble:** Averaged multi-seed Gradient Boosting (3 configs) + Extra Trees + Random Forest predictions over all training data. The top-5 slots were stable across all 15 model runs (c006, c017, c021, c031 in top-5 in 15/15 runs; c014 in 9/12 of the weighted runs).

- **c006** – tempering 450 °C, starter/composition-type (Ni 0.6, Mn 0.8, Ti 0.2, Si 0.8, Cu 0.3), no aging
- **c017** – tempering 300 °C, same strong composition, no aging
- **c021** – tempering 200 °C, same strong composition, no aging
- **c031** – tempering 500 °C, same composition, no aging
- **c014** – tempering 450 °C, lean composition (Ni 0, Mn 0.4, Si 0.4), no aging

Runners-up: c018 (~870 MPa predicted) and c015 (~864).

Final: c006, c017, c021, c031, c014

**Data overview:** The training set (300 samples, targets 177–1900 MPa) covers many steel families.
